provider: Debian Salsa (salsa.debian.org) - GitLab with Generic package registry

free_tier.stated: No published total-storage quota, but a fully published per-object table on the instance-configuration page. Package registry per-file caps: Generic 5 GiB, Conan 3 GiB, Maven 3 GiB, PyPI 3 GiB, Terraform 1 GiB, npm/NuGet 500 MiB, Helm 5 MiB. Core GitLab: max push size '-' (unlimited), max attachment 20 MiB, job artifact 750 MiB, pages 300 MiB, snippet 50 MiB, import remote file 10 GiB, download file 5 GiB.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

retention.stated: per-object-cap: 5 GiB per Generic package file; 750 MiB per CI artifact; 300 MiB Pages. retention: indefinite for packages and repos (no pruning policy published on this page)

egress.terms: Free. Debian-hosted infrastructure with no billing, no per-GB meter, and package/registry downloads served straight from the instance. No Cloudflare dependency to worry about.

tooling: Full GitLab: `git` over SSH/HTTPS, GitLab Generic Package API (`PUT /projects/:id/packages/generic/:package_name/:version/:file_name`), CI runners, `glab`/`lab` CLIs, `python-gitlab`. Max push size is '-' (unlimited) which is the interesting cell - the per-object cap is on the *registry*, not on git.
chaining: Unlimited projects per account x 5 GiB per Generic-package file x unlimited files per package version x unlimited versions. Plus unlimited-size git pushes as a second surface. The binding limit is account creation, not storage.

reliability_note: Manual registration review is the whole story - it converts account-farming from an API call into a queue measured in days, which is fatal for the 'unlimited free orgs' pattern that made the Google-Drive-service-account trick work. Once in, the surface is clean and standard GitLab. Public read is fine (project pages and package downloads are anonymous).

extras.agent_focus: The code-forge seam: OSS project hosts, software-download directories, game/mod distribution and mirror services. Question for each: (a) any published byte quota, (b) is upload possible over SFTP/rsync/SCP/SSH rather than a web form, (c) is there a public download CDN, (d) does it need an approved project or can any account create one, (e) per-file cap. Round 2 flagged that SourceForge has no published quota and serves over plain SFTP with a global mirror CDN, and that an rclone-backend enumerator would score the niche as empty. This slot tests that class systematically. Every number below was read live or from a dated archive capture this session.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
